key_insight: The paper shows that efficient wrapper-based feature selection can improve wind and solar power prediction by identifying the most useful inputs and reducing noise. In practice, this can make renewable energy forecasts more accurate and computationally efficient.
problem_solved: Renewable energy output is highly variable because it depends on weather and environmental conditions. This paper addresses the challenge of building reliable wind and solar power prediction models from complex, high-dimensional data.
method: Conducted two structured literature reviews focused on real-world wind and solar power forecasting.
Analyzed wrapper-based feature selection methods that evaluate feature subsets using model performance.
Compared efficient selection strategies to understand how they can improve predictive accuracy and reduce unnecessary input variables.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the study highlights a practical way to improve forecasting models without simply adding more data. It is especially relevant for energy applications where accuracy, interpretability, and efficiency all matter.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing raw weather data -> feature selection -> forecasting model -> power prediction
Side-by-side comparison chart of model performance with and without feature selection
Icon set for wind turbines, solar panels, weather variables, and AI model
Feature ranking graphic highlighting the most important predictors
paper_title: Improving Wind and Solar Power Prediction with Efficient Wrapper-based Feature Selection: An Empirical Study
paper_authors: Daniel Grillmeyer, Marius Hadry, Michael Stenger, Vanessa Borst, Veronika Lesch
